headline: Apple posts, then pulls, listing for its own AI agent
dek: TechCrunch and The Verge report the removed listing described an assistant that runs a computer on its own.

s2.label: What happened
s2.title: The listing that vanished
body: Apple posted an engineering listing to lead an AI agent that operates a computer on its own, then removed it from its site (TechCrunch, The Verge).
Bloomberg first spotted the listing, according to TechCrunch.

s3.label: How it works
s3.title: What the agent would do
s3.body: The posting described a system that picks the right tool at each step.

points.t: Handles web browsing and moves between apps (TechCrunch).
Runs commands and writes and fixes code (TechCrunch).
The role would report into Siri and Foundation Models teams (The Verge).

s4.label: Why it matters
s4.title: A race already underway
body: Meta, Google, OpenAI and Anthropic have launched agents that take over computer tasks, TechCrunch reports.
Apple is tightening third-party agent access to the Mac (TechCrunch).

items.t: Apple has considered launching the agent by the end of next year (TechCrunch).
The project remains in its early stages, TechCrunch says.
Apple is weighing letting Siri organize Safari tabs on its own (The Verge).

caption.hook: Apple wants an AI agent that runs a computer on its own.
body: Apple posted and then pulled a listing for an engineer to lead an AI agent that can browse the web, use apps, run commands and write code, according to TechCrunch and The Verge. Bloomberg first spotted it. The role would sit inside the Siri and Foundation Models teams.

Meta, Google, OpenAI and Anthropic already have agents that take over computer tasks (TechCrunch). Meanwhile Apple is tightening third-party agent access to the Mac. Bloomberg found Apple considered a launch by the end of next year, but the project is still early (TechCrunch).
caption.cta: Should Apple build its own computer-using agent or stay out of the race?
